features: INSTALMENTS FALL DUE WHEN YOU SAY — An administrator's own words: «in the instalment plan, how do I set the first instalment to a specific date? By default it takes the start of the accounting period». He was not asking for a convenience: he was describing a behaviour he was subjected to. Three administrators asked for it, and he was right — the start date was hardwired to the management period's start in three places in the code.
DATABASE MIGRATION: one new column, data_prima_scadenza on piani_rate, nullable. No existing data is touched and no plan changes behaviour.

THE INSTALMENT PLAN NOW HAS A «FIRST DUE DATE» FIELD. Leave it empty and the plan starts from the beginning of the management period exactly as before, and the screen tells you which date it would use. Empty is not missing data: it is the choice to follow the management period. A plan without its own date moves if the period's start moves; whoever wants it fixed sets a date. That is why the column was not backfilled on existing plans: filling it would have frozen them on a date computed today, turning a live default into a dead copy.

The chosen date keeps its own day: if you say «the first instalment on 30 September», the first due date is the 30th and not the 5th. From the second one onwards the day of the month takes over, which is what indicating a day actually means.

Fixed — THE DUE DAY WAS BORN ON THE 1ST OF THE MONTH INSTEAD OF THE 5TH. Anyone who did not specify the day got a plan falling due on the first, while the database schema declares the fifth: a value written in the code never let the default speak. Plans created without specifying the day of the month have their instalments on day 1, and are corrected by setting the day and recalculating.

Fixed — THE CALENDAR REMINDER COULD DUPLICATE ITSELF. The check that prevents creating the same event twice also keyed on the instalment's date, while the instalment is already identified by its own number. As long as due dates never moved this made no difference; from this release they move, and without the fix every move would have left the old event in the calendar alongside the new one.

Under the hood: the rule «where the calendar starts» now exists in two languages, because the interface must be able to show it before saving, and it is pinned by two twin test suites over the same cases — the pattern that in beta.35 cost a one-cent divergence on the net payable. Synchronising due dates onto the quotas was not built, and that is the right call: changing the date requires a recalculation, the recalculation deletes and regenerates the instalments, and the quotas die with their instalment, so divergence is impossible — there is now a test pinning that, because it will become possible once already-generated dates can be edited. Twenty-two new tests, seven of them in JavaScript.
